report_name: AI-Powered Hacking Tools Like CyberStrikeAI Used in Japan Attacks

attack_patterns.name: Gather Victim Host Information
attack_patterns.description: The CyberStrikeAI framework performed automated reconnaissance to gather information about target hosts by scanning public sources and using asset discovery tools as part of its attack sequence against Japanese organizations.

attack_patterns.name: Vulnerability Scanning
attack_patterns.description: The CyberStrikeAI framework performed automated vulnerability scanning as part of its reconnaissance phase against Japanese organizations.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: The CyberStrikeAI framework was used to exploit common vulnerabilities for initial access. A separate human-led campaign also targeted exposed VPNs and Oracle WebLogic servers.

attack_patterns.name: Application Layer Protocol
attack_patterns.description: A dedicated AI agent within the CyberStrikeAI framework managed command and control communications during the attacks on Japanese organizations.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
attack_patterns.description: An AI agent in the CyberStrikeAI framework automated the process of identifying and exfiltrating valuable data from victim networks, likely over web services.

attack_patterns.name: Resource Hijacking
attack_patterns.description: In one campaign, attackers compromised a GIS server to steal its computing resources to power their own AI workflows.

attack_patterns.name: Default Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Attackers compromised a geographic information system (GIS) server using default credentials to hijack its computing resources.

tools.name: CyberStrikeAI
tools.description: An open-source AI penetration testing framework that uses a swarm of 44 AI agents to automate the entire attack lifecycle, from reconnaissance to data exfiltration. It was used in a campaign against at least 19 organizations, primarily in Japan.

campaigns.name: CyberStrikeAI Automated Attack Campaign
campaigns.description: A fully automated attack campaign conducted in October 2026 using the CyberStrikeAI framework against at least 19 organizations, primarily in Japan.
campaigns.objective: Automated compromise and data exfiltration from multiple organizations.

campaigns.name: Human-Led AI-Assisted Campaign
campaigns.description: A campaign conducted between January and October 2026 where a human operator used AI as an assistant to develop custom attack tools and scripts for targeting exposed VPNs and web servers.

campaigns.name: Infrastructure Hijacking for AI Workflows Campaign
campaigns.description: A campaign in August-September 2026 where attackers compromised a GIS server using default credentials to steal computing resources for their own AI workflows.
campaigns.objective: Theft of computing resources for AI workflows.

infrastructure.name: Hijacked GIS Server
infrastructure.description: A geographic information system (GIS) server that was compromised via default credentials. Its computing resources were hijacked by attackers to power their own AI workflows.

indicators.name: Automated Exploit Framework User-Agent
indicators.pattern:
title: Automated Exploit Framework User-Agent
id: 2b9c1f8a-7d3e-4b1f-8c9a-0d1e2f3a4b5c
status: experimental
description: Detects User-Agent strings associated with automated scanning or exploitation frameworks, potentially used by AI-driven attack tools like CyberStrikeAI.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/cyberstrikeai-uses-44-ai-agents-to.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-28
tags:
  - attack.t1595
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.reconnaissance
  - attack.initial_access
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-useragent|contains:
      - 'sqlmap'
      - 'nmap'
      - 'metasploit'
      - 'CyberStrikeAI'
      - 'commix'
      - 'wpscan'
      - 'nessus'
      - 'nuclei'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: This rule detects HTTP User-Agent strings commonly associated with automated penetration testing and vulnerability scanning tools. The presence of such user agents could indicate reconnaissance or exploitation attempts by automated frameworks like CyberStrikeAI.
